blocks.en: The Turning Point: Bread, Confession, and Glory
blocks.es_reference: El punto de giro: pan, confesión y gloria

blocks.en: The Feeding of the Five Thousand, the Bread of Life, Caesarea Philippi, and the Transfiguration
blocks.es_reference: La alimentación de los cinco mil, el Pan de vida, Cesarea de Filipo y la transfiguración

blocks.en: 1. The Bread That Multiplied
blocks.es_reference: 1. El pan que se multiplicó

blocks.en: A great crowd had followed Him into a lonely place, and as the day wore on they grew hungry. Jesus, who saw them with a shepherd's heart (Mark 6:34), would not send them away empty. A boy had five barley loaves and two small fish — "but what are they among so many?" (John 6:9). He took the little that was offered, gave thanks, broke it, and gave; and "they all ate and were filled" (Matthew 14:20). Twelve baskets of fragments were gathered up, more left over than they had begun with, and those who ate were about five thousand men besides women and children (Matthew 14:21). The little that is placed in His hands is never too little. It is the only miracle of His ministry told in all four Gospels — a sign too large to leave out.
blocks.es_reference: Una gran multitud lo había seguido a un lugar apartado, y al avanzar el día tuvieron hambre. Jesús, que los veía con corazón de pastor (Marcos 6:34), no quiso despedirlos vacíos. Un muchacho tenía cinco panes de cebada y dos pececillos — “mas ¿qué es esto entre tantos?” (Juan 6:9). Tomó lo poco que se le ofreció, dio gracias, lo partió y lo dio; y “comieron todos, y se saciaron” (Mateo 14:20). Se recogieron doce cestas de pedazos, más de lo que tenían al comenzar, y los que comieron eran como cinco mil hombres, sin contar las mujeres y los niños (Mateo 14:21). Lo poco que se pone en sus manos nunca es demasiado poco. Es el único milagro de su ministerio que cuentan los cuatro Evangelios — una señal demasiado grande para omitir.

blocks.en: But watch what the crowd did with it. "This is truly the Prophet who is to come into the world," they said, and they were "about to come and take Him by force to make Him king" (John 6:14–15). They wanted a bread-king — a Messiah of full stomachs and broken Roman chains. So He withdrew to the mountain alone. The sign was meant to point past the bread to the Bread; the crowd stopped at the loaves.
blocks.es_reference: Pero observe lo que la multitud hizo con ella. “Este verdaderamente es el Profeta que había de venir al mundo,” dijeron, y estaban “para venir y tomarle por fuerza para hacerle rey” (Juan 6:14–15). Querían un rey-pan — un Mesías de estómagos llenos y cadenas romanas rotas. Por eso se retiró al monte, solo. La señal había de apuntar más allá del pan al Pan; la multitud se detuvo en los panes.

blocks.en: 2. The Bread of Life
blocks.es_reference: 2. El Pan de vida

blocks.en: The next day they hunted Him down — for more bread. He named it plainly: "you seek Me, not because you saw the signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were filled" (John 6:26). "Do not labor for the food which perishes," He told them, "but for the food which endures to everlasting life" (John 6:27). And then He spoke the first of His great I AM words: "I am the bread of life. He who comes to Me shall never hunger, and he who believes in Me shall never thirst" (John 6:35).
blocks.es_reference: Al día siguiente lo buscaron — por más pan. Él lo dijo claramente: “me buscáis... porque comisteis el pan y os saciasteis” (Juan 6:26). “Trabajad,” les dijo, “no por la comida que perece, sino por la comida que a vida eterna permanece” (Juan 6:27). Y entonces pronunció la primera de sus grandes palabras YO SOY: “Yo soy el pan de vida; el que a mí viene, nunca tendrá hambre; y el que en mí cree, no tendrá sed jamás” (Juan 6:35).

blocks.en: They had reminded Him that Moses gave their fathers manna in the wilderness (John 6:31); He answered that the true bread comes down from heaven and gives life to the world (John 6:33). "Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, and are dead," He said; "this is the bread which comes down from heaven, that one may eat of it and not die... if anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever" (John 6:49–51). The manna fed the body for a day; the living Bread feeds the soul forever.
blocks.es_reference: Le habían recordado que Moisés dio a sus padres el maná en el desierto (Juan 6:31); Él respondió que el verdadero pan desciende del cielo y da vida al mundo (Juan 6:33). “Vuestros padres comieron el maná en el desierto, y murieron,” dijo; “este es el pan que desciende del cielo, para que el que de él comiere, no muera... si alguno comiere de este pan, vivirá para siempre” (Juan 6:49–51). El maná alimentó el cuerpo por un día; el Pan vivo alimenta el alma para siempre.

blocks.en: Here is a thing worth pausing over. It is possible to want what Jesus gives without wanting Jesus — to love the loaves and never love the Lord. A child may love a father only for the coins in his pocket, and feel nothing for the father himself; and the moment the coins stop, the affection stops. So it was with the crowd. They came for bread, and when the bread ran out and the words grew hard, they left.
blocks.es_reference: He aquí algo en que detenerse. Es posible querer lo que Jesús da sin quererlo a Él — amar los panes y nunca amar al Señor. Un hijo puede amar a su padre solo por las monedas de su bolsillo, sin sentir nada por el padre mismo; y en cuanto cesan las monedas, cesa el cariño. Así fue con la multitud. Vinieron por pan, y cuando el pan se acabó y las palabras se hicieron duras, se fueron.

blocks.en: For the words did grow hard: "unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink His blood, you have no life in you" (John 6:53). He did not mean a literal eating — He explained it Himself: "It is the Spirit who gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words that I speak to you are spirit, and they are life" (John 6:63). To eat and drink Him is to come to Him and believe on Him, to feed on Him by faith. But the saying was too much for the bread-seekers: "From that time many of His disciples went back and walked with Him no more" (John 6:66). The crowd had thinned to the committed. Jesus turned to the Twelve: "Do you also want to go away?" And Peter answered for them all: "Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life" (John 6:67–68).
blocks.es_reference: Porque las palabras sí se hicieron duras: “si no coméis la carne del Hijo del Hombre, y bebéis su sangre, no tenéis vida en vosotros” (Juan 6:53). No quiso decir un comer literal — Él mismo lo explicó: “El espíritu es el que da vida; la carne para nada aprovecha; las palabras que yo os he hablado son espíritu y son vida” (Juan 6:63). Comerlo y beberlo es venir a Él y creer en Él, alimentarse de Él por la fe. Pero el dicho fue demasiado para los buscadores de pan: “Desde entonces muchos de sus discípulos volvieron atrás, y ya no andaban con él” (Juan 6:66). La multitud se había reducido a los comprometidos. Jesús se volvió a los Doce: “¿Queréis acaso iros también vosotros?” Y Pedro respondió por todos: “Señor, ¿a quién iremos? Tú tienes palabras de vida eterna” (Juan 6:67–68).

blocks.en: 3. Caesarea Philippi: The Great Confession
blocks.es_reference: 3. Cesarea de Filipo: la gran confesión

blocks.en: Far to the north, He drew the question to a point. First the easy one: "Who do men say that I, the Son of Man, am?" — and they reported the rumors: John the Baptist, Elijah, Jeremiah, one of the prophets (Matthew 16:13–14). Then the sharp one, the question every soul must finally answer: "But who do you say that I am?" (Matthew 16:15).
blocks.es_reference: Lejos, al norte, llevó la pregunta a un punto. Primero la fácil: “¿Quién dicen los hombres que es el Hijo del Hombre?” — y reportaron los rumores: Juan el Bautista, Elías, Jeremías, alguno de los profetas (Mateo 16:13–14). Luego la aguda, la pregunta que toda alma debe al fin responder: “Y vosotros, ¿quién decís que soy yo?” (Mateo 16:15).

blocks.en: Peter spoke the confession at the heart of the faith: "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God" (Matthew 16:16). Jesus called him blessed, for "flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but My Father who is in heaven" (Matthew 16:17), and said, "on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it" (Matthew 16:18) — the rock being this confessed truth of who He is, the foundation no power of death can overcome. To them He gave "the keys of the kingdom of heaven" (Matthew 16:19) — the authority to open its door to the world by the gospel they would preach.
blocks.es_reference: Pedro pronunció la confesión que está en el corazón de la fe: “Tú eres el Cristo, el Hijo del Dios viviente” (Mateo 16:16). Jesús lo llamó bienaventurado, porque “no te lo reveló carne ni sangre, sino mi Padre que está en los cielos” (Mateo 16:17), y dijo: “sobre esta roca edificaré mi iglesia; y las puertas del infierno no prevalecerán contra ella” (Mateo 16:18) — siendo la roca esta verdad confesada de quién es Él, el fundamento que ningún poder de muerte puede vencer. Les dio “las llaves del reino de los cielos” (Mateo 16:19) — la autoridad de abrir su puerta al mundo por el evangelio que predicarían.

blocks.en: And then, the moment the disciples knew who He was, He told them what He had come to do: "From that time Jesus began to show His disciples that He must go to Jerusalem, and suffer many things... and be killed, and be raised the third day" (Matthew 16:21). It was the first plain word of the cross. Peter recoiled and rebuked Him — and drew the sharpest answer in the Gospels: "Get behind Me, Satan!... you are not mindful of the things of God but the things of men" (Matthew 16:23). It was the wilderness temptation again, in a friend's voice: a crown without a cross. Then He laid the road before them all: "If anyone desires to come after Me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow Me" (Matthew 16:24). For, He went on, "whoever desires to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake will find it. For what profit is it to a man if he gains the whole world, and loses his own soul?" (Matthew 16:25–26). The way up is down; the way to keep your life is to spend it on Him.
blocks.es_reference: Y entonces, en el momento en que los discípulos supieron quién era, les dijo lo que había venido a hacer: “Desde entonces comenzó Jesús a declarar a sus discípulos que le era necesario ir a Jerusalén y padecer mucho... y ser muerto, y resucitar al tercer día” (Mateo 16:21). Fue la primera palabra clara de la cruz. Pedro retrocedió y le reprendió — y recibió la respuesta más cortante de los Evangelios: “¡Quítate de delante de mí, Satanás!... no pones la mira en las cosas de Dios, sino en las de los hombres” (Mateo 16:23). Era la tentación del desierto otra vez, en voz de un amigo: una corona sin cruz. Luego puso el camino delante de todos: “Si alguno quiere venir en pos de mí, niéguese a sí mismo, y tome su cruz, y sígame” (Mateo 16:24). Porque, prosiguió, “todo el que quiera salvar su vida, la perderá; y todo el que pierda su vida por causa de mí, la hallará. Porque ¿de qué aprovecha al hombre, si ganare todo el mundo, y perdiere su alma?” (Mateo 16:25–26). El camino hacia arriba es hacia abajo; el modo de guardar la vida es gastarla en Él.

blocks.en: 4. The Transfiguration
blocks.es_reference: 4. La transfiguración

blocks.en: Six days later He took Peter, James, and John up a high mountain, and "He was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, and His clothes became as white as the light" (Matthew 17:1–2). For a moment the veil of His flesh was drawn back, and the glory of the eternal Word blazed through the man. Moses and Elijah appeared and spoke with Him (Matthew 17:3) — the Law and the Prophets, both bearing witness to Him; and Luke tells us they spoke of His "decease which He was about to accomplish at Jerusalem" (Luke 9:31). Even on the mount of glory, the talk was of the cross.
blocks.es_reference: Seis días después tomó a Pedro, Jacobo y Juan a un monte alto, y “se transfiguró delante de ellos; y resplandeció su rostro como el sol, y sus vestidos se hicieron blancos como la luz” (Mateo 17:1–2). Por un momento se descorrió el velo de su carne, y la gloria del Verbo eterno resplandeció a través del hombre. Moisés y Elías aparecieron hablando con Él (Mateo 17:3) — la Ley y los Profetas, ambos dando testimonio de Él; y Lucas nos dice que hablaban de su “partida que iba Jesús a cumplir en Jerusalén” (Lucas 9:31). Aun en el monte de la gloria, se hablaba de la cruz.

blocks.en: Peter, dazzled, wanted to build three tents and stay (Matthew 17:4). But a bright cloud overshadowed them, and the Father's voice came as it had at the Jordan: "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Hear Him!" (Matthew 17:5). The Father confirmed the Son and added a command — hear Him — especially in the hard word about the cross that Peter had just tried to wave away. The disciples fell on their faces in terror; Jesus touched them and said, "Arise, and do not be afraid." And when they looked up, they saw "no one but Jesus only" (Matthew 17:7–8). Moses would die and Elijah had been carried to heaven, yet neither was the resting place: the voice did not say "hear Moses" or "hear Elijah," but Hear Him. When the cloud lifted, the Law and the Prophets had stepped back, and the disciples saw Jesus only — for to Him they had always pointed. The glory faded; the Son remained; and the road led back down the mountain, toward Jerusalem.
blocks.es_reference: Pedro, deslumbrado, quería hacer tres enramadas y quedarse (Mateo 17:4). Pero una nube de luz los cubrió, y la voz del Padre vino como en el Jordán: “Este es mi Hijo amado, en quien tengo complacencia; a él oíd” (Mateo 17:5). El Padre confirmó al Hijo y añadió un mandato — oídle — sobre todo en la palabra dura de la cruz que Pedro acababa de querer apartar. Los discípulos cayeron sobre sus rostros con terror; Jesús los tocó y dijo: “Levantaos, y no temáis.” Y al alzar la vista, no vieron “a nadie sino a Jesús solo” (Mateo 17:7–8). Moisés moriría y Elías había sido llevado al cielo, pero ninguno era el lugar de reposo: la voz no dijo “oíd a Moisés” ni “oíd a Elías,” sino a él oíd. Cuando la nube se levantó, la Ley y los Profetas se habían retirado, y los discípulos vieron a Jesús solo — pues a Él siempre habían apuntado. La gloria se desvaneció; el Hijo permaneció; y el camino bajaba del monte, hacia Jerusalén.

blocks.en: 5. The Hinge of the Gospel
blocks.es_reference: 5. El gozne del evangelio

blocks.en: This is the great turning point. He had revealed Himself as the Bread of Life; the crowds had been sifted down to the few; the Twelve had confessed Him as the Christ; and the Father had confirmed Him in blazing glory. Yet through all of it the shadow lengthened: the talk now turned to suffering, to being killed, to the decease He would accomplish at Jerusalem. The mountaintop was real, but it was not the destination; the destination was a hill outside the city walls.
blocks.es_reference: Este es el gran punto de giro. Se había revelado como el Pan de vida; las multitudes habían sido cribadas hasta los pocos; los Doce lo habían confesado como el Cristo; y el Padre lo había confirmado en gloria resplandeciente. Y sin embargo, a través de todo, la sombra se alargaba: ahora se hablaba de padecer, de ser muerto, de la partida que cumpliría en Jerusalén. El monte fue real, pero no era el destino; el destino era una colina fuera de los muros de la ciudad.

blocks.en: And the divine/human pattern stands at its sharpest here. As God He multiplied bread for thousands and shone like the sun on the mountain; as man He was abandoned by the crowd and set His face toward death. The same Jesus is the Bread that is broken and the Glory that is veiled. He asks of us what He asked then: not to seek Him for the loaves, but to confess Him as the Christ and follow Him — down the mountain, and on to the cross.
blocks.es_reference: Y el patrón divino/humano está aquí en su punto más agudo. Como Dios multiplicó pan para miles y resplandeció como el sol en el monte; como hombre fue abandonado por la multitud y puso su rostro hacia la muerte. El mismo Jesús es el Pan que se parte y la Gloria que se vela. Nos pide lo que pidió entonces: no buscarlo por los panes, sino confesarlo como el Cristo y seguirlo — monte abajo, y hacia la cruz.

sa.prompt: Describe the feeding of the five thousand and what the crowd misunderstood about it.
sa.model: From a boy's five loaves and two fish, Jesus fed about five thousand men, and twelve baskets of fragments were gathered, more than they began with. It is the only miracle in all four Gospels. But the crowd wanted to make Him a bread-king by force; they stopped at the loaves instead of seeing the sign point to the Bread. The little placed in His hands proved more than enough.

sa.prompt: Explain “I am the bread of life” and how Jesus contrasted Himself with the manna (John 6).
sa.model: Jesus declared, “I am the bread of life,” the first of His great I AM sayings; whoever comes to Him never hungers and whoever believes never thirsts. Unlike the manna their fathers ate in the wilderness and still died, this living bread comes down from heaven and gives eternal life, so that whoever eats of it will live forever. He is the food that endures, not the food that perishes.

sa.prompt: What did Jesus mean by “eat My flesh and drink My blood” (John 6:53-63)?
sa.model: Jesus said unless one eats His flesh and drinks His blood he has no life, but He explained He did not mean literal eating: the Spirit gives life, the flesh profits nothing, and His words are spirit and life. To eat and drink Him is to come and believe, feeding on Him by faith. The hard saying sifted the crowd; many disciples turned back, but Peter said He has the words of eternal life.

sa.prompt: What does the sifting of the crowd (John 6:66-68) show about true discipleship?
sa.model: When the words grew hard, many who had followed for the loaves went back and walked with Him no more. The crowd was sifted down to the committed few. Jesus asked the Twelve, “Do you also want to go away?” and Peter answered, “Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life.” True discipleship clings to Christ for who He is, not merely for what He gives.

sa.prompt: What happened at Caesarea Philippi, and what did Peter confess (Matt 16:13-18)?
sa.model: At Caesarea Philippi Jesus first asked who men said He was, then the sharper question: “But who do you say that I am?” Peter confessed, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” Jesus said the Father had revealed this, not flesh and blood, and that on this rock — the confessed truth of who He is — He would build His church, which the gates of Hades could not overcome.

sa.prompt: Explain the first passion prediction and Jesus' rebuke of Peter (Matt 16:21-23).
sa.model: As soon as the disciples knew who He was, Jesus began to tell them He must go to Jerusalem, suffer, be killed, and rise the third day — the first plain word of the cross. Peter rebuked Him, and Jesus answered, “Get behind Me, Satan,” because Peter was minding the things of men, not of God. It was the wilderness temptation again: a crown without a cross.

sa.prompt: Explain the cost of discipleship in Matthew 16:24-26.
sa.model: Jesus laid the road before all: whoever would come after Him must deny himself, take up his cross, and follow. Whoever tries to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for His sake will find it; for what does it profit a man to gain the whole world and lose his soul? Discipleship is cruciform — the way up is down, and we keep our life by spending it on Him.

sa.prompt: Describe the Transfiguration and what it confirmed (Matt 17:1-5).
sa.model: On a high mountain Jesus was transfigured: His face shone like the sun and His clothes became white as light, the glory of the eternal Word blazing through the man. Moses and Elijah, the Law and the Prophets, appeared and spoke of His coming death at Jerusalem. The Father's voice said, “This is My beloved Son... Hear Him,” confirming the Son and commanding obedience even in the hard word of the cross.

sa.prompt: What did the Father's command “Hear Him” and “Jesus only” mean (Matt 17:5-8)?
sa.model: Peter wanted to build three tents and stay, but the Father's voice commanded, “Hear Him.” The command was not to hear Moses or Elijah but Jesus, especially in the hard word about the cross Peter had resisted. When the cloud lifted they saw Jesus only — the Law and the Prophets had pointed to Him and now stepped back. The glory faded, but the Son remained, and the road led toward Jerusalem.

sa.prompt: Why is this part of the ministry called the turning point of the Gospel?
sa.model: This is the hinge of the Gospel. Jesus revealed Himself as the Bread of Life, the crowds were sifted to the few, the Twelve confessed Him as the Christ, and the Father confirmed Him in glory — yet through it all the shadow of the cross lengthened, with talk of suffering and death at Jerusalem. As God He fed thousands and shone like the sun; as man He set His face to die. He asks us to confess Him and follow Him to the cross.
